# Improve the way the work is done

It is easy to finish a task and repeat the same costly mistake on the next one.
AI-Forward treats improvement as a loop: observe what happened, identify the recurring
shape, propose a useful change, review it, and turn it into a control that will matter
when the situation recurs.

This is not a requirement to write a retrospective after every small edit. It is a
way to avoid paying repeatedly for problems that the team already understands.

## Measure before optimizing

“The agent was slow” is not yet a diagnosis. Time may have gone into useful reasoning,
repeated context loading, waiting for a tool, duplicated research, unnecessary reviews,
or a build that repeatedly initializes the same expensive resource.

[Session profiling](#skill-session-profiler) uses available local telemetry to
separate these possibilities. Check which harnesses and fields the current profiler
actually supports. A missing measurement should remain missing, not turn into a
plausible estimate presented as fact.

```text
/session-profiler Review the authorized HarborTasks sessions from this week.
Find repeated reads, avoidable handoffs and tool waits. Separate measured findings
from estimates, and propose fixes without changing the project.
```

Use `$session-profiler` in Codex where the workflow is installed. Invoking it from
a harness does not imply that harness's telemetry is supported by the analysis.

## Treat context as a budget

Instructions, tool definitions, prior messages and files all occupy context. Carrying
an unrelated task into a long session can make every later step more expensive and
harder to focus. More context is not always more useful context.

Keep tasks scoped, read the information needed for the decision, and preserve durable
project knowledge rather than relying on an ever-growing conversation. A new task may
deserve a fresh session. Specialist agents should carry the context needed for their
work rather than receive every project document.

Model choice also belongs to the task. Novel design and adversarial review may need
different capability from mechanical regeneration or a bounded command. Prefer
deterministic tooling where a model adds no useful judgment.

## Do not equate parallelism with a saving

Parallel work helps only when the branches can progress independently and the
coordination cost is justified. Two agents editing the same contract may spend
more time resolving contention than one agent would spend completing the change.

[Optimize the execution graph](#skill-optimize-graph) when the work has enough
dependencies, branching or repetition to warrant it. Shorten unnecessary chains
before adding more workers. Keep budgets and a real stopping condition.

For HarborTasks, agreeing on the export's row-selection contract is a dependency
for both backend and UI work. Running those decisions independently is not useful
parallelism; it produces competing answers to the same question.

## Understand cost honestly

Provider pricing and account models differ. A subscription, a metered API and a
credit-based plan do not expose cost in the same way. Do not infer a precise spend
from elapsed time, token counts without the applicable billing model, or a requested
model name that was not confirmed at execution.

Use the measurements the host provides, state what they mean, and keep missing data
explicit. The pack's commercial/cost guidance helps reason about the shape of the
cost; it is not a permanently current price list.

The same discipline applies to CI: measure expensive setup and contention before
adding runners or cutting checks. A faster gate that no longer proves the important
behavior is not an improvement.

## Turn an incident into a reusable lesson

Suppose the export lost tasks after the first page. The useful lesson is not
“remember to fix this export.” It is “a test using a hand-built list did not exercise
the real paging boundary.”

Look for siblings, derive shared behavior where possible, and add a check that fails
on the broken shape. Keep the result in the project's defect-class knowledge so
future work can find the reason for the control.

[Dream](#skill-dream) consolidates committed project history into proposed learning
for human review. It is not an autonomous policy updater. Accepted, generalized
learning can be reconciled into other repositories with
[apply-learnings](#skill-apply-learnings), which produces reviewable plans rather
than silently executing them.

## A practical improvement loop

1. Collect the permitted measurements and current project records.
2. Separate observations from hypotheses.
3. Choose the few changes that address repeated, meaningful cost or failure.
4. Review the proposed change and its consequences.
5. Implement an approved control with a check that can fail.
6. Measure whether the problem recurs.

Do not optimize for a cleaner-looking report. A useful improvement makes the work
more reliable or removes unnecessary effort without weakening a necessary safeguard.

or [maintain the pack deliberately](#maintain).
